Lesson 1

What ARE Nail Dashes?

Luxury press-ons with an average wear time of 10+ days. These are not your average drugstore press-ons! They're tapered at the cuticle and curved to hug your nail bed.

They're also a one-step manicure: no waiting for 3 to 5 layers of polish to dry. If the kids need you halfway through, get up and help, then sit back down and finish. Nothing smudges. #WINWIN

Lesson 2

💡 Fun fact: keeping up acrylic nails at the salon costs at least about $1,400 a year, before any special designs or extras. 🤯

Salon acrylics$1,400+
Nail Dashes$390–450

The Nail Dashes number assumes you never reuse a single set.

Lesson 3

Not all press-ons are created equal

A good press-on won't bend, break or snag your hair. Sound familiar? 😩

  • Curved to hug your nail bed for a better seal and longer wear. Drugstore press-ons are flat and flimsy.
  • Tapered and curved down at the cuticle, so goodbye hair snags.
  • Fits deeper nail beds, not just short ones.
Lesson 4

How to get 1 to 2+ weeks of wear

Press-ons that last need three things:

  1. Proper nail prep. Rubbing alcohol isn't enough for most people. Use a nail dehydrator or 100% acetone (unless your nail beds are naturally dry).
  2. The right glue technique. HOW you apply the glue matters just as much as the glue itself: a thin layer on your nail AND the back of the Dash, apply at a 45° angle, then press and hold 60 to 90+ seconds.
  3. A good quality press-on. If yours bend, break or snag your hair, you need better press-ons. That's where we come in! 😉💅

Bonus

The Hybrid Method

Sticky tabs ON the nail, plus a drop of glue at the cuticle. If you tend to rip your nails off instead of soaking them, this one is for you!

I do this when I only want about a week of wear, but I don't want my nails wiggling, pushing into my cuticle or snagging my hair on the tabs.

  1. Prep like normal (rubbing alcohol AND dehydrator).
  2. Pick the largest sticky tab that fits your nail bed.
  3. Apply the tab and warm it by rubbing with your finger for about 30 seconds.
  4. Peel the plastic off the tab and add a dot of glue at the cuticle area.
  5. Press and hold the Dash for about 90 seconds.

You get good wear, and they still come off easily in 3 to 5 days. Let Karli know if you try it!

Lesson 5

Will they fit my nails?

Every box comes with plenty of sizes (newer styles have extended sizing), so you'll find your fit.

  • Petite nail beds: start with a short square.
  • Wide nail beds: just wear the larger sizes in the box. Length doesn't change the width.
  • Extra long nail beds (cuticle to tip): try a medium length.
  • Want them shorter or a different shape? Dashes are easy to clip and file.

Lengths come in petite (little girls ages 7 to 12), short, medium, long and extra long. Each color or design comes only in the length and shape you see, with a small handful of exceptions. So if you love a blue short square, grab it in short square!

Not sure which length to try? Send Karli a picture of your nails for a recommendation.
Lesson 6

The collections

  • 🩷 Classics: the OG Nail Dashes, in tons of designs and seasonal collections.
  • 💜 The POP: looks and wears just like the Classics, but the nails and packaging are made from recycled materials. Known for edgy, super trendy designs.
  • 🤍 Acrylics: extra layers make them thicker, for the look and feel of salon acrylics. Neutral, classic salon looks with a high gloss.
  • Bitten: edgy, extra-long ballerina and stiletto shapes.
  • Besties: 3 matching sets to share with your bestie or someone special.
  • Aspen Blossom: designed by kids, for kids, with petite sizes and nail tabs instead of glue.
"Are the Acrylics better?" It's personal preference! Acrylics hold up to the most abuse because they're thicker, but not everyone likes the thickness. Love a natural feel, like dip or shellac? Go Classics. Love your salon acrylics? Go Acrylic.
Lesson 7

Gentle removal

Proper removal keeps your nail beds healthy. No acetone soak! All you need is a bowl of warm water, dish soap and oil (cuticle oil or olive oil works great).

  1. Break the seal around the edge of each Dash. The Nail Dash removal tool works great for this.
  2. Apply oil to your nails, ideally over the bowl of warm, soapy water.
  3. Soak for 10 to 20 minutes, gently prying at the Dashes every few minutes.

It should never hurt or take force. Having trouble? Add more oil and soak a little longer.

Lesson 8

Do press-ons damage your nails?

This is the question I get most, and the answer is no. Damage only comes from improper removal, or from wearing sets back to back.

Give your nails a 24 to 48 hour break between sets, and use that time for some TLC:

  • Cuticle oil: use it while you wear your Dashes AND on bare nails between sets. Argan, jojoba, grapeseed and rosehip oils.
  • Cuticle remover: softens and dissolves dead skin for a salon-quality finish at home.
  • Cuticle pusher: dual-sided stainless steel, one end to push back cuticles and one for precise cleanup.
  • Hand cream and hand masks: hands are one of the fastest-aging areas of the body, especially in dry winter months.
